============================================================================================
CROSS-MODAL GRAPHEME<->PHONEME (graph-native): reading aloud. Vision (Omniglot/PointSetDist) and
speech (FSDD/DtwTo) share the AbS spine; a co-presented pair binds grapheme<->phoneme. Recall is bidir.
============================================================================================

  taught 10/10 grapheme<->phoneme pairs by co-presentation (exact binding).

  cross-modal recall                          accuracy
    READ ALOUD  (new writer: symbol -> sound)       80.0%   (40 held-out graphemes)
    DICTATION   (new speaker: sound -> symbol)       70.0%   (40 held-out phonemes)

  ========================================================================================
  reading aloud and taking dictation are graph-native (cross_modal Rules over the shared concepts);
  vision and speech use the SAME AbS argmax. Read-aloud rides the strong grapheme channel; dictation
  rides the harder speaker-independent speech channel -- both far above chance (10%). The two
  perception arcs (writing + speech) are now one system, bound graph-native by co-presentation.
============================================================================================
